- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.7) — model tends to overshoot bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows when sentiment turns negative or weak (e.g., <0.5) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Model exhibits lagged mean reversion: forecasts often peak 2–3 days before true price drops, especially after sentiment spikes.
- Overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment >0.9 followed by drop) — model overreacts and fails to correct.
- Forecast bias is stronger in 30-day horizon: model consistently overpredicts early in the window, then underpredicts late — align with sentiment decay.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating 0.9 and 0.1), model fails to adjust — forecasts remain anchored to recent highs.
- Correct for sentiment-driven momentum: if sentiment drops below 0.4, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in downward drift.
